jobs.title: Chief Scientist
jobs.description: **The Opportunity:** Lead deep\-water ecological research from an operational offshore platform. MARÉ provides what academic labs often lack: a dedicated ROV fleet, a 20\-year benthic imagery archive, and a skilled engineering and video processing team ready to turn field operational data into high\-impact peer\-reviewed science. **Position Overview:** Since 2003, Marine Applied Research \& Exploration (MARÉ) has been putting (robotic) eyes on the seafloor below diver depth \- typically in the mid\-depth 30m to 500m range. We are seeking a Chief Scientist to serve as MARÉ’s primary scientific authority, driving our research agenda across mesophotic ecosystems, deep\-sea coral/sponge communities, and seamount ecology along the North American West Coast, the Gulf of Mexico, and beyond. This is an applied research and expedition leadership role designed for an active marine ecologist. Rather than managing bureaucracy or driving advocacy campaigns, you will focus on high\-caliber science: acting as Chief Scientist on multi\-week offshore ROV missions, publishing peer\-reviewed research, collaborating closely with video processing and engineering teams to modernize ocean data extraction, and building scientific partnerships across North American and global deep\-sea networks (including NOAA, state fisheries departments, and academic research institutions). **Key Responsibilities:** * **Expedition Leadership \& Field Science:** Plan, direct, and serve as Chief Scientist on multi\-week offshore ROV expeditions, overseeing cruise track design, dive planning, biological sampling protocols, and real\-time dive scientific reporting. Survey Design \& Rigor: Establish and maintain robust scientific sampling standards and QA/QC protocols for all video\-derived transects, bathymetric characterizations, and oceanographic data collections. Permitting \& Compliance: Lead scientific permitting processes for state, federal, and international offshore operations in collaboration with operations staff. * **Scientific Research \& Collaborative Publishing:** Author and co\-author high\-impact research papers in peer\-reviewed journals, positioning MARE’s long\-term observational datasets within broader oceanographic and ecological literature. Archive Science: Tap into MARE’s extensive 20\-year imagery archive to identify novel research questions, historical baseline comparisons, and ecological trends in mesophotic and seamount communities. * **External Scientific Synthesis and Conference/Network Visibility:** Serve as the primary technical point of contact for external scientific collaborators (e.g., NOAA Deep Sea Coral Research and Technology Program, state agency scientists, university partners), facilitating open data exchange and joint proposal writing. Present research findings at major national and international ocean science conferences and represent MARÉ in deep\-sea working groups. Developing opportunities for collaboration with other mission\-aligned NGOs and topic\-aligned academic institutions. * **Data Modernization \& Technical Collaboration:** Work closely with MARÉ’s internal video processing team and software engineer to refine species identification pipelines, taxonomy keys, and biological database structures (SQL/GIS), working with them to continuously improve the speed and quality of marine data processing workflows with the latest technological advancements. Collaborate with scientific partners to integrate MARÉ data into larger data systems. **Qualifications:** Required Experience: * Ph.D. in Marine Biology, Biological Oceanography, Marine Ecology, or a closely related discipline. Deep\-Water Expertise: Demonstrated research focus and publication record in mesophotic (30m–150m), deep sea coral, seamount, or benthic ecology below diver depth. * Sea Time \& ROV Experience: Proven track record serving as Chief Scientist, Co\-Chief, or Lead PI on multi day/multi\-week offshore research cruises involving ROVs, submersibles, or advanced benthic survey platforms. * Analytical \& Spatial Skills: Strong quantitative background in ecological statistics, spatial analysis (GIS), and handling large observational or imagery\-derived ecological datasets. * Excellent communication and collaboration skills, and an action\-orientation to turn exploration into rigorous and relevant scientific research into pragmatic conservation and restoration outcomes. * Work Authorization: Candidates must be currently authorized to work in the United States and not require current or future employer sponsorship. Preferred Experience: * ROV piloting and/or navigating experience. * Familiarity with Eastern Pacific (North American West Coast) mid\-depth ecosystems.. * Established scientific network with federal agencies (NOAA Fisheries / Sanctuaries), state marine resource agencies, or deep\-sea research consortia. * Demonstrated success in writing or co\-authoring scientific grant proposals (e.g., NOAA, NSF, state research grants, or research foundations). * Experience with machine learning tools for ocean imagery processing (e.g., automated species classification, 3D habitat reconstruction). **How to Apply:** * Please send to MARÉ Executive Director, Larissa Pommeraud () a cover letter detailing your motivation and availability (time and office presence) with your offshore ROV/expedition leadership experience and research interests, as well as a complete CV with publication list, and contact information for 2\-3 professional references. Pay: $95,000\.00 \- $115,000\.00 per year Benefits: * 401(k) * 401(k) matching * Dental insurance * Flexible schedule * Health insurance * Paid time off * Retirement plan * Vision insurance Application Question(s): * How soon could you start? Education: * Doctorate (Required) Experience: * mid\-depth marine ecology field research and analysis: 3 years (Required) Ability to Relocate: * Blue Lake, CA 95525: Relocate before starting work (Preferred) Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Code With Your Explanation (Paid Data Task, Remote, Contract)
jobs.description: **ABOUT KLED** Kled is building the largest opt\-in human data network in the world. We are not a labeling firm. We are not a task marketplace. We are a consumer application where people upload their real photos, videos, and documents and get paid continuously. We then filter, standardize, and license that data to frontier AI labs and enterprises that need fresh, rights\-aware training data. Since launching our mobile app in 2026, we have: * Reached \#1 on the App Store (Finance) with 0 paid marketing * Scaled to 600,000\+ active data contributors * Processed 5M uploads per day * Raised $15M\+ from investors behind SpaceX, Airbnb, Coinbase, xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Spotify, Lyft, Uber, and more Our mission is to let anyone download the app and earn a real living wage from uploading their data. This listing is for one paid task in the Kled app: "Code With Your Explanation". There is no interview and no minimum hours: download the app, open the task, and you are paid per accepted submission. ### **What you will do** Paste in code you wrote, a script, a function, a query, a spreadsheet formula, then explain what it does and why you built it that way. ### **Steps** * Paste code you wrote yourself * Explain what it does * Explain why you built it that way, and what approach you rejected * Submit ### **What gets rejected** * Do not paste code you did not write * Do not skip the reasoning stage * Do not submit two\-line snippets Accepted: Code you wrote yourself, plus an explanation of both what it does and why you chose that approach. ### **Pay** $7\.00 per accepted sample. At a typical pace of about 12 minutes per sample, that is about $35 per hour. One sample takes about 12 minutes and pays $7\.00\. One sample per contributor. You are paid per accepted submission (piecework, independent contractor); submissions that break the rules are not paid. Payouts are made in the app (PayPal, Venmo or a Solana wallet). ### **Where and when** Open worldwide: the task runs in 100\+ countries. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position. ### **What you need** * An iPhone running iOS 18\.6 or later (the Kled app is iPhone\-only right now) * 18 or older * Your own writing, typed in the app ### **How to start** * Download Kled from the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/kled/id6752585718 (also at kled.ai/app). * Create your account and open Tasks. * Search "Code With Your Explanation", read the brief and follow the on\-screen steps. * Submit. Accepted submissions are paid in the app. Every submission is reviewed, and you opt in to a commercial training license on each upload; accepted submissions are licensed to AI labs. Questions: support@kled.ai.

jobs.title: Connected Systems Architect – Manufacturing & OT
jobs.description: **Shape the backbone of connected engineering at Kform** -------------------------------------------------------- Step into a typical day: you review an overnight change proposal in Git, verify automated tests for a network segmentation update, and walk the manufacturing floor to validate a new edge gateway talking to a PLC and a test stand. Back at your workstation, you refine Ansible playbooks and Terraform/OpenTofu modules, then pair with a software engineer to finalize an API mapping into ERP and quality systems. In the afternoon, you meet cybersecurity to confirm logging and access boundaries for controlled technical data, document the rollout plan and rollback path, and finish by updating runbooks and diagrams before the change window. ### **What you’ll do** * Design end\-to\-end physical and logical architectures across offices, labs, production lines, and customer or field sites — including on‑premises, edge, and intermittently connected scenarios. * Configure and administer switches, firewalls, Wi‑Fi, servers, endpoints, gateways, identity and access services, and related infrastructure. * Define segmentation, routing, addressing, access paths, and data flows bridging enterprise IT, operational technology (OT), test systems, and external services. * Treat infrastructure, networks, access, and deployments as versioned code wherever practical; build automation for provisioning, configuration, validation, backup, and recovery. * Use Git\-driven reviews and change control to test, approve, document, and reproduce system changes; maintain baselines with clear rollback options. * Integrate machines, sensors, controllers, edge computers, and test equipment with engineering, ERP, quality, and other business applications; specify interfaces and coordinate custom APIs/services with internal developers and vendors. * Establish device onboarding, asset inventory, configuration, patching, monitoring, backup, and recovery practices that respect uptime, equipment constraints, and operator safety. * Safeguard controlled unclassified and export\-controlled information via sound boundaries, access controls, logging, and evidentiary documentation in partnership with cybersecurity and program owners. * Troubleshoot across networks, operating systems, devices, automation, and application interfaces; validate integrations in labs and on the manufacturing floor. * Keep diagrams, inventories, interface definitions, configuration records, runbooks, and change documentation current; support quality management system processes. * Plan deployments, manage dependencies, and resolve issues alongside manufacturing, engineering, quality, cybersecurity, software, and IT partners. ### **Minimum qualifications** * Bachelor’s in IT, Computer/ Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field; or equivalent proven experience. * Hands\-on experience designing, administering, and troubleshooting networked infrastructure and systems. * Deep fluency with TCP/IP, switching, routing, VLANs, DNS, DHCP, firewalls, and network segmentation. * Practical experience with infrastructure as code, configuration management, and scripting/automation; comfortable managing definitions and changes in Git and debugging both automation and the underlying infrastructure. * Administration experience with Windows and/or Linux, identity and access, monitoring, backups, and recovery. * Background integrating physical devices/equipment with networked and application ecosystems, including defining and validating interfaces and data flows. * Ability to own an infrastructure or integration change from architecture through implementation, validation, documentation, and operational handoff. * Clear technical writing and cross‑disciplinary troubleshooting across IT and OT. ### **Preferred qualifications** * Experience with Ansible, Terraform or OpenTofu, PowerShell, Python, or similar automation stacks. * Familiarity with industrial networks, machine connectivity, PLCs, SCADA, MES, manufacturing test systems, or edge gateways. * Experience integrating CAD/PLM, ERP, quality, manufacturing, and test systems via vendor interfaces, APIs, and data exchange. * Background in defense, aerospace, advanced manufacturing, or other settings handling controlled information. * Knowledge of NIST SP 800‑171, CMMC, NIST SP 800‑82, and documenting technical controls and audit evidence. * Experience with secure or government clouds, Microsoft 365 GCC High, and hybrid architectures. * Comfort with disconnected/intermittent environments and constrained patch or maintenance windows. ### **Skills and working style** * Translate operational, security, and production goals into practical, reliable architectures. * Write maintainable automation, review and test changes, and restore known‑good configurations when needed. * Balance security with reliability, continuity, and human safety. * Collaborate on interfaces and integrations without needing to build full‑stack applications. * Explain boundaries, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and non‑technical stakeholders. * Own problems to resolution and leave systems and documentation better than you found them. ### **Working conditions** * Mix of desk work and hands‑on activity across labs, manufacturing areas, and occasional customer/field sites. * Standing, walking, connecting equipment, installing hardware, and using tools may be part of your day. * Personal protective equipment may be required during installation, testing, and manufacturing activities. ### **Other expectations** * Align with Kform’s values: ownership, teamwork, and continuous improvement. * Handle sensitive program information per company and customer requirements. * Support planned maintenance, integration, deployment, and incident response outside standard hours when necessary. ### **Core proficiencies** * IT equipment across servers, networks, telecom, and cloud platforms. * Network connectivity fundamentals (TCP/IP, SD‑WAN).

jobs.title: Data Engineer, Ingestion Platform
jobs.description: **Location** ------------ Remote **Employment Type** ------------------- Full time **Location Type** ----------------- Remote **Department** -------------- Product and Data **Compensation** ---------------- * $155K – $165K • Offers Equity Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading\-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real\-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform. **The Role** ------------ Alt Value is our moat. It is only as good as the data underneath it — and that data lives on dozens of external marketplaces and auction houses that have no interest in making it easy for us to get. That's this job. You own the pipelines that scrape, normalize, and land every transaction and listing that feeds our pricing model. When a comparable sale closes on eBay or at a major auction house, how fast it shows up in Alt Value, and whether it shows up correctly, is your call and your consequence. Pricing decisions, cash advance terms, market analytics, and every dashboard in the company sit downstream of you. **The metric you own: Data Coverage.** Supporting KPIs are pipeline latency, uptime, and source coverage. **What You'll Own:** -------------------- * **The ingestion layer.** Design, optimize, and own the pipelines that scrape, process, and ingest transaction and listing data from major auction houses and marketplaces. Scraper to orchestrator to warehouse, end to end. * **Build for reuse first.** Most of the ingestion stack — auth handling, retries, session and proxy management, monitoring — should generalize across sources. Go deep and custom only where a specific source's structure actually requires it. * **Knowing before we do.** Build the monitoring and alerting that tracks latency, uptime, and coverage across every source. A source going quiet should page you, not surprise a pricer three days later. * **Making it cheaper and steadier.** Modernize storage and processing, cut manual intervention out of the loop, and optimize for cost, performance, and reliability. * **The consumers.** Partner with pricing, ML, product, and analytics to deliver data clean and standardized enough that nobody downstream is writing defensive code around your output. **How You'll Use AI Here:** --------------------------- We don't want to hear that you use Claude every day. Everyone does. We want to know what you've built with it. Concretely, in this role: * Point an agent at a **site that just changed its markup** and have it propose the parser fix, run it against a fixture set, and open the PR * Build a **triage loop over the orchestrator** — cross\-reference a failed DAG against logs and warehouse state, diagnose the cause, and hand you a ranked list instead of a wall of red * Use **LLM extraction for the long tail** of low\-volume sources where a bespoke scraper will never pay for itself * Put an **MCP server over the warehouse** so a coverage question is a sentence, not another one\-off query * Use **Claude Code or Cursor** as the default way you work through a migration or a backfill, not as autocomplete If you've built agents, written skills or MCP servers, wired up connectors, or shipped internal tooling your team actually depends on — lead with that. **What You Bring:** ------------------- * 3\-4 years in data engineering or a closely adjacent seat. * Modern web scraping at scale — Playwright or comparable, plus the ability to impersonate a real browser at the network layer (TLS/request fingerprinting) when a plain HTTP client gets flagged. Selenium alone doesn't cut it anymore. * Strong Python, 3\+ years hands\-on. Solid SQL for analysis and transformation. * A pipeline you owned end to end in the past two years. Not a pipeline you contributed to. One that was yours when it broke. * Judgment on when to generalize and when to go bespoke — you don't rebuild the same infrastructure per source, and you don't force a one\-size\-fits\-all approach onto a source that needs custom handling. * Orchestration in your hands, not your resume. Airflow, Dagster, or a comparable DAG system — you've built on it, been paged for it, and cleaned up after it. * Cloud development experience (AWS, GCP). * LLM\-based extraction and processing at scale (e.g. LLM\-as\-a\-Judge, Agent loops), not just UI\-based Q\&A and simple Skill building. * Startup experience. You understand the pace, and you've worked somewhere the roadmap changed under you. * A pragmatic bias. Value delivered incrementally over the perfect rebuild. **Bonus:** large\-scale dataframe processing (Pandas, Polars, PySpark). You collect, or you have opinions about the collectibles market. **How We'll Interview You:** ---------------------------- We'll be specific so you can prepare. *Before any of it: download the app, put a card up, make a bid, or put a card up for sell. Every round assumes you've used the product, and we expect your point of view to sharpen as you go.* **1\. Recruiter screen \- 30 minutes** Come ready to talk about the metric you own today, why Alt specifically, and how you're actually using AI. We'll answer your questions and align on comp. **2\. Hiring manager with Dae, Head of Data — 30 minutes.** Be ready to go deep on one pipeline you owned end to end: the systems design, what you owned versus the team, where it broke, and what came out the other side. **3\. Coding screen — 45 minutes.** A working session on a data problem close to what this role actually does. **4\. Systems design — 60 minutes.** Design an ingestion system under real constraints. We'll push back on at least one of your choices on purpose — how you take that matters as much as the design. **5\. Cross\-functional — 60 Mins** How you work with the people downstream of your data. **6\. Leore, our founder and CEO — 30 minutes.** Everyone who joins Alt meets Leore. Come with a point of view on what you'd go after first. **7\. Reference check(s) — 15 minutes** with a former manager(s) **Compensation:** $155,000 \- $165,000 per year, plus equity for all full\-time employees. **What we offer:** ================== ***For full\-time Employees*** * We cover 85% of your medical, dental, and vision, and up to 50% for dependents. HSA/FSA available * Generous PTO that people actually take * Parental leave at full salary * $200/month wellness \+ $100/month home office stipend * Free DoorDash Pass membership, because dinner shouldn't be a decision * Remote\-first (for most positions), with WeWork access when you want a room with other humans * 401(k) * Alt Equity to all full\-time employees Compensation Range: $155K \- $165K

jobs.title: Principal Electrical Engineer
jobs.description: *Aerospace is at a turning point — costs are rising, supply chains are strained, and old ways of building can't keep up. At Neon Aero, we're breaking that mold. We move fast, think big, and combine start\-up agility with aerospace expertise to design, build, and scale aircraft in ways the industry has never seen. Our team leverages automation, AI\-driven tools, and a fully connected digital backbone to accelerate innovation and reduce barriers to production.* *Here, you won't just take a job — you'll help reinvent how the world flies. If you're ready to solve complex problems, push technology further, and work alongside some of the brightest minds in aerospace, this is your chance to make a real impact.* We are seeking a Principal Electrical Engineer to provide technical leadership in the architecture, design, and qualification of high\-integrity electronic control systems across Neon's product portfolio. This role is focused on the controller and system\-electronics side of the architecture: command/monitor architecture, flight control computers and LRUs, embedded compute, sensing, communications, fault detection, redundancy, and the electrical interfaces that tie complex products together. It is complementary to our Principal Engineer – High Voltage Power Electronics role, which owns high\-voltage motor\-drive and power\-stage design. This is a deeply hands\-on individual contributor role. You will develop system architectures, block diagrams, schematics, interface definitions, safety concepts, and the analysis behind them. You will work directly with embedded software, motor control, systems, mechanical, power electronics, test, manufacturing, and certification teams to bring high\-reliability electronic systems from concept through qualification and production. This role does not require direct people management, but it requires principal\-level technical leadership, mentoring, and ownership of difficult cross\-functional decisions. **Why This Role Matters** * Own electrical system architecture for high\-integrity controller electronics, FCCs, LRUs, actuator controllers, avionics/compute platforms, sensing systems, and related embedded hardware. * Architect command/monitor, active\-active, simplex, duplex, or other redundant control architectures based on system safety, integrity, availability, and cost requirements. * Define partitioning between command processors, monitoring processors, motor\-control electronics, power electronics, sensors, communications, and vehicle\-level interfaces. * Translate system requirements and safety objectives into practical electronic architectures, hardware requirements, interface definitions, and verification strategies. * Select microcontrollers, processors, FPGAs, memories, communication devices, supervisors, watchdogs, isolation components, and sensor interfaces appropriate for high\-reliability applications. * Design and review embedded digital, analog, and mixed\-signal electronics, including low\-voltage power supplies, power sequencing, reset architecture, discrete I/O, signal conditioning, protection, and health monitoring. * Architect fault detection, fault containment, redundancy management, cross\-monitoring, heartbeat, synchronization, and safe\-state mechanisms. * Define communication architecture and physical layers for interfaces such as CAN / CAN FD, ARINC 825, ARINC 429, Ethernet, RS\-422/485, SPI, and similar embedded or aerospace buses. * Own electrical interface definitions and collaborate with systems and software teams on ICDs, timing assumptions, diagnostic coverage, degraded modes, and hardware/software partitioning. * Establish grounding, shielding, isolation, EMI/EMC, signal\-integrity, and power\-integrity approaches across boards, harnesses, sensors, and enclosures. * Lead schematic development and critical PCB design reviews using Altium or equivalent ECAD tools. * Personally perform or direct worst\-case circuit analysis, tolerance analysis, derating, signal\-integrity analysis, power\-budget analysis, and fault analysis. * Lead board bring\-up, system integration, lab debugging, and root\-cause investigations for issues spanning hardware, firmware, software, sensors, communications, and power electronics. * Define hardware verification strategies and support qualification testing for environmental, EMC, electrical power, and fault conditions. * Support certification\-oriented development including requirements traceability, design assurance, configuration control, verification evidence, and hardware change management. * Drive DFM, DFT, DFA, production test strategy, and manufacturing readiness for controller electronics and LRUs. * Mentor electrical engineers through architecture reviews, schematic reviews, design analysis, bring\-up, and debugging while remaining deeply hands\-on. **Qualifications** * Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or related field; equivalent professional experience may be considered. * 12\+ years of experience developing and shipping complex electronic systems. * Demonstrated ownership of system\-level electrical architecture for embedded control, avionics, industrial control, automotive, robotics, medical, aerospace, or similarly high\-reliability products. * Deep hands\-on experience with embedded digital and mixed\-signal hardware, including microcontroller\-based systems, sensing, communications, and board\-level power architecture. * Strong proficiency with schematic capture and PCB design using Altium or equivalent ECAD tools. * Strong understanding of processor selection, watchdog and reset architecture, communication interfaces, sensor interfacing, low\-voltage power conversion, grounding, isolation, and EMI/EMC. * Experience designing fault\-tolerant or redundant electronic architectures and reasoning about failure detection, fault containment, and safe\-state behavior. * Experience bringing electronic assemblies from concept through prototype, qualification, industrialization, and production. * Proven ability to lead cross\-functional technical decisions involving electrical hardware, embedded software, systems engineering, mechanical design, test, manufacturing, and suppliers. * Strong lab and debugging capability using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, programmable supplies, electronic loads, data acquisition, and related instrumentation. **Preferred Experience** * Command/monitor or other redundant safety\-critical controller architectures. * Flight control computers, actuator controllers, avionics LRUs, embedded compute platforms, sensor interfaces, or vehicle\-control electronics. * DO\-254 hardware development experience and familiarity with DAL\-driven hardware architecture and verification. * Familiarity with DO\-160, ARP4754A/B, ARP4761, MIL\-STD\-461, MIL\-STD\-704, or comparable safety\-critical and environmental standards. * Experience with CAN / CAN FD, ARINC 825, ARINC 429, Ethernet, RS\-422/485, SPI, BiSS, resolver/LVDT interfaces, or similar sensing and communication technologies. * Experience with safety\-oriented or aviation\-pedigree microcontrollers and processors. * FPGA or programmable\-logic experience for monitoring, I/O, timing, or safety functions. * MATLAB, Python, SPICE, or similar tools for analysis, test automation, or data reduction. * Experience in aerospace, automotive, robotics, consumer hardware, industrial controls, medical devices, or other environments where electronics must be both high\-performance and production\-ready. **Why Join Us** * Work alongside elite engineering talent and innovators from across aerospace and tech. * Be part of a team moving faster than the industry standard. * Shape solutions that are lower\-cost, autonomous, and scalable: the future of aviation. * Competitive compensation, including equity participation, growth opportunities, and full health benefits (health, vision, dental, 401(k)) designed to support you in and out of work. *Neon Aero, Inc is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law.* *We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation, and we welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply.* *All final candidates must successfully complete a background check and drug screening as a condition of employment.* **At this time, Neon Aero and its divisions are not accepting unsolicited resumes from third\-party recruiters or staffing agencies.**

jobs.title: Product Builder, Growth
jobs.description: **Location** ------------ Remote **Employment Type** ------------------- Full time **Location Type** ----------------- Remote **Department** -------------- Product and Data **Compensation** ---------------- * $200K – $250K • Offers Equity Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading\-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real\-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform. **The Role** ------------ Alt is growing! This role leads the charge on new user count: how many collectors land on Alt, how many make a first submission or a first bid, and how many come back without being asked. That number is the job. Everything else in this description is downstream of it. **This is a builder seat, not a product management seat.** You own the seller submission funnel, buyer search and discovery, and the experimentation infrastructure underneath both, and you own them the whole way: you find the drop\-off, you write the code, you ship it behind a flag, you read the result, you keep it or you kill it. **What this role is not:** writing PRDs for someone else to implement, running roadmap ritual, managing a pod, or translating between engineering and the business. If that's the shape of your last five years, this probably isn't the right fit, and we'd rather say so up front than waste your time. **What it is:** pulling the funnel yourself in SQL on Monday, shipping the onboarding change on Tuesday, standing up the experiment harness that makes Wednesday's test trustworthy, and putting a model behind dealer reactivation instead of a campaign. You report directly to the CEO. If you want a CEO in the build with you, this is that. If you want distance from the top, it isn't. **The metrics you own: Submission Volume (weekly, by seller segment) and Search\-to\-Bid Conversion.** Supporting KPIs: Snap to Sell activation rate on first submission, seller reactivation rate among dormant sellers, daily active search query volume, listing rate (vaulted inventory live on marketplace), ship\-and\-decide velocity (changes shipped and tests called per week), and dealer segment submission frequency and GMV. The people who are great at this have run growth inside a system that was already working, not just inside a roadmap someone else set. They ship their own code. And they are participants in this market: they buy, they sell, and they have a view on where liquidity actually goes. **What You'll Own** ------------------- * **The submission funnel, end to end, in code.** From a seller's first submission to a high\-frequency, high\-value one. Find the drop\-offs across onboarding, Snap to Sell, quote acceptance, vault intake, and resubmission, then ship the fixes yourself. Build the experiences that activate dormant sellers and raise dealer submission frequency without anyone having to send a message. * **Search, discovery, and buyer conversion.** Search quality, card discovery, and browse across the platform. Move search\-to\-bid through ranking, filtering, recommendations, and real\-time Alt Value pricing context. You'll be in the ranking code, not describing it. Right card, right buyer, right moment. * **The experimentation harness.** Build it, don't request it. Assignment, exposure logging, guardrails, readouts, and decision rules, wired to the warehouse and fast enough that a test is a Tuesday decision. Then run high\-velocity tests on it across onboarding, activation, search, and submission, and leave behind a compounding library of what we learned. * **Marketplace liquidity and supply\-demand balance.** Watch submission volume, listing rate, bid depth, and sell\-through. Find the imbalances by card category, price tier, and seller segment, then build the product that fixes them. Use Alt Value as a growth lever: surface the market signal that makes someone act. * **The bets and the trade\-offs.** A short quarterly plan tied to submission volume, buyer conversion, and time\-to\-liquidity, and a weekly record of what actually shipped. Work shoulder to shoulder with Engineering, Design, Data, Lifecycle, and Ops. Operate on the funnel detail and the experiment result, and on which bets we're making and why. Communicate the trade\-offs to the CEO plainly. **What Great Looks Like (6 Months)** ------------------------------------ * **You've been shipping to production since week two**, and the team reviews your PRs the way they review each other's. * **Weekly submission volume is measurably up**, driven by changes you built rather than by headcount or outreach. * **An experimentation harness you built** carrying 3 to 5 concurrent tests across growth surfaces, trusted enough that people stop arguing about the numbers. * **Snap to Sell activation rate meaningfully improv an read code." You open the pull request, you take the review, you own the on\-call consequence. Full\-stack enough to move through a growth surface without a handoff: the frontend flow, the API, the query, the job. * **You've owned a growth surface, marketplace funnel, or PLG motion** and moved the number on it. Roughly 5\+ years of building, but we're reading the work, not the years. * **You own a number today** and can name it, its baseline, and where you took it, on the first ask. * **Strong data fluency.** SQL and Python, plus PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Statsig, Eppo, or similar. You pull your own numbers and you've built the instrumentation behind them. * **Experimentation in your hands, not on your résumé.** You've designed the test, set the decision rule before it ran, and made the call on partial data. * **Deep understanding of two\-sided marketplace dynamics.** Supply and demand, liquidity, and what happens to one side when you push the other. * **You've built real things with AI**, not just used it. Agents, skills, MCP servers, connectors, internal tooling people depend on. * **Scrappy and high\-ownership.** You communicate with precision, you move without hand\-holding, and you go find the problem rather than waiting for the brief. **This Probably Isn't For You If** ---------------------------------- * You need requirements to arrive before you can start. * Your best work happened inside a well\-run PM, design, and engineering machine, and you're looking for a more structured one. * You'd hand the prototype to an engineer. Here, the prototype is how the argument gets settled, and you build it. * You're excited to manage before doing. This is a builder's role first. The org grows around people who deliver. * You want to own the roadmap more than the outcome. **How We'll Interview You:** ---------------------------- We'll be specific so you can prepare. *Before any of it: download the app, put a card up, make a bid, or sell. Every round assumes you've used the product, and we expect your point of view to sharpen as you go.* **1\. Recruiter screen\- 30 minutes via google meet.** The metric you own today, the last thing you shipped yourself, why Alt specifically, and how you're actually using AI. We'll answer your questions and align on comp. **2\. Hiring manager with Leore, our founder and CEO, 30\-45 minutes.** This role reports to Leore, so he runs the hiring manager round himself. Go deep on a funnel you owned: the baseline, where you took it, what you built, and the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't. **3\. Team Interview, 2\- 45 Minutes sessions.** The engineers and data partners you'll ship alongside. How you work in a shared codebase. **4\. Build walkthrough\- 45\-60 minutes.** Bring one thing you built and shipped, a repo, a PR, a live URL, an internal tool, an agent or skill you wrote, and open it on screen. What problem it solved, what's ugly about it, where AI helped and where it got it wrong. Then we go deep on a funnel you owned: the baseline, where you took it, what you shipped. Rough and real beats polished and hypothetical. **5\. Executive interview, 30 minutes.** The closing conversation. What you'd go after first, what you'd deliberately not do, and whether this is the job you actually want. **6\. Reference check(s), 15 minutes** with a former manager(s) **Compensation:** $200,000 \- $250,000 per year, plus equity for all full\-time employees. **What we offer:** ================== ***For full\-time Employees*** * We cover 85% of your medical, dental, and vision, and up to 50% for dependents. HSA/FSA available * Generous PTO that people actually take * Parental leave at full salary * $200/month wellness \+ $100/month home office stipend * Free DoorDash Pass membership, because dinner shouldn't be a decision * Remote\-first (for most positions), with WeWork access when you want a room with other humans * 401(k) * Alt Equity to all full\-time employees Compensation Range: $200K \- $250K

Today too much of that path runs on people: manual approvals, hand\-checked disbursements, a triage queue that grows when a transfer goes sideways, and screens that don't always tell the borrower where their money is. Your job is to turn that into a product. You'll implement our new underwriting design hand in hand with our data scientists, automate the loan workflow end to end, own disbursement failures until they stop happening, and ship the borrower and operator experiences on top, built from our designs. The north star: T7 (trailing 7\-day) Disbursement within SLA rate, with a target of 99%. Every underwriting change, automation, triage fix, and screen you ship either moves that number or protects it. Supporting KPIs: time from application to underwriting decision, share of loans that go from application to funded with no manual touch, disbursement exceptions per week, and support tickets asking "where is my money," driven toward zero. In lending, a disbursement that "probably went out" is a failure. The people who are great at this have owned a lending or payments product where it mattered, from the state machine to the pixels. They think in idempotency and reconciliation because they've been on the wrong side of both, and they care that the UI tells the truth about what the system is doing. ### **WHAT YOU'LL OWN** * **The underwriting revamp.** We're redesigning how we underwrite cash advances and term loans, and you'll implement the new design end to end, working hand in hand with our data scientists. That means turning their models and credit policy into a production decisioning service: inputs computed reliably, every decision versioned and explainable, and every rule or model change shipped through shadow mode and backtests before it goes live. Done looks like the new logic deciding every application, with Data Science able to iterate on it without an engineering rewrite. * **The automated loan workflow.** Application, underwriting decision, offer, acceptance, disbursement, servicing, repayment, delinquency, and collateral release, modeled as an explicit state machine with every transition logged. Manual steps become rules, and rules become auditable. Done looks like a standard advance funding with no human in the loop, and a non\-standard one landing in front of the right person with the context already attached. * **Disbursement triage, fixed at the root.** Failed, duplicated, delayed, and stuck disbursements. Done looks like the triage queue shrinking week over week, with the T7 SLA rate to prove it. * **The borrower experience, built to design.** The cash advance offer, acceptance, disbursement status, repayment, payoff, and loan history screens across web and mobile, implemented faithfully from our designs and improved through what you learn in production. You own design fidelity, accessibility, and performance, and you make sure the status a borrower sees is the status the loan is actually in. * **Operator and triage tooling.** The internal console where Credit, Operations, and Support see every loan and disbursement, spot the stuck ones, and resolve them with the context already on screen. packages, comprehensive benefits. We provide a supportive and inclusive work environment where your skills and expertise can make a significant impact on the safety and security of our communities. **Lovelace’s founding team includes:** **Andrew Moore**, who has a track record of building impactful AI systems, designing them with human rights impact assessments as a top priority, leading the AI division of one of the world’s foremost cloud companies, and actively participating in machine learning and AI research over the past two decades. **Toby Smith**, well known in the Pittsburgh Tech community for his engineering leadership and design skills, and who has led many of the most ambitious and complex system infrastructure projects in Google Pittsburgh and NetApp. Here is a note from Andrew Moore to people who are reading these Job Postings: “Hi folks, I’m so glad you are potentially interested in Lovelace AI. jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Full Stack (Agentic Payment)
jobs.description: **About Sapiom** Sapiom is payment infrastructure for AI companies and agents. One integration lets an agent pay on behalf of a person or a business, with permissions, protected card credentials, and spending rules built in. Agents can think now, and increasingly they can act. What they can’t do is spend. The rails underneath assume a person at the keyboard, so teams fall back on closed catalogs, cards and API keys pasted into config, or a human approving every purchase. We’re removing that constraint. A customer connects a card and grants a named agent permission without leaving your product. They set the limits — per purchase, per merchant, approval required or not. The agent buys inside those limits across browser checkout, payment protocols, and APIs. Card details never enter the conversation, and every purchase leaves a record from approval through merchant confirmation. The work spans the whole path a purchase takes: connecting a customer and their agent, vaulting the card, establishing agent identity, enforcing the rules, moving the payment, and making the outcome legible afterward. Card issuing, voice\-initiated payments, payment recovery, and insurance are all part of where this goes. We have assembled a team with deep infrastructure and payments DNA. Our founder ran payments engineering at Shopify for five years and built an autonomous consumer agent company before that. We raised a $35M Series A led by Dragonfly in August, bringing us to $50M total. Accel led our seed; Menlo Ventures and Anthropic are also behind us. **About the role** ------------------ Agents are starting to buy things on their own, and the rails underneath all assume a person at the keyboard. Letting an agent complete a purchase inside limits its owner actually set, and keeping proof of what was agreed, is the company. The first version of that ships before you'd start. Almost everything that turns it into something customers can depend on is still ahead, and the team works those problems in parallel rather than one at a time. You'd own one of them. Payments is unforgiving in a way most product work isn't. A purchase either moves money or it doesn't. A record either holds up six months later when someone disputes a charge, or it's worthless. We'd like someone who finds that interesting. This is a staff role. You'd set the design for a large piece of this, at thirty people, while it's still deciding\-shaped. **What you'd work on** ---------------------- **Limits and authority.** How much latitude an owner hands an agent, and how that gets enforced before money moves rather than explained afterwards. Most of these decisions are still open. **Completing the purchase.** Checkout is where this gets unglamorous. Every merchant behaves differently, totals move, and plenty of steps still expect a human. Making that reliable across a long tail of them is a multi\-quarter problem. **What happens when it goes wrong.** A payment that goes quiet is the hardest case in the domain. The system has to work out what actually happened before it does anything else, and never charge someone twice. **Proof.** A versioned record of what a buyer saw and agreed to, still legible months later when someone disputes it. Unglamorous, and the thing the rest of it rests on. **The surface customers build on.** A public API and the tools an agent calls. Designing a contract a model uses correctly is its own discipline. **You may be a fit if** ----------------------- * You have 8\+ years building production software, several of them in payments, money movement, or financial infrastructure. We're hiring for depth in the domain. * You've owned architecture from first principles — set the design, defended it, and lived with what it cost. * You've worked somewhere being wrong was expensive, and you design for failure up front: idempotency, retries, reconciliation against a number someone else is also computing. * You have real range across the stack. Strong TypeScript, and you build the interface on top of your own system instead of handing that off. * You've run a multi\-month project from a problem statement rather than a spec, and other engineers built on what you shipped. * You use AI tools in your own engineering workflow. Nice to have: card issuing, tokenization, or PCI scope; checkout integrations at depth; browser automation or request interception; something you shipped that an LLM calls as a tool; early\-stage companies where you set the architecture rather than inherited it. **Applying** ------------ A recruiter screen, then a loop of roughly three hours: a hands\-on AI project, a project deep dive, and a conversation with our founder. Everyone on our engineering team carries the title Member of Technical Staff internally.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Ledger
jobs.description: **Location** ------------ Remote **Employment Type** ------------------- Full time **Location Type** ----------------- Remote **Department** -------------- Product and Data **Compensation** ---------------- * $300K – $500K • Offers Equity Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading\-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real\-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform. **THE NORTH STAR** 99\.99% reliability on gateway and banking integrations, and a ledger where every cent is accounted for and every entry says who created it and when. Supporting KPIs: reconciliation exception queue depth at daily close, gateway and banking integration uptime at 99\.99%, P90 time from auction close to seller funds available, share of ACH returns and reversals handled with no manual correcting entry, and time to bring a new PSP or rail to production. **TH ROLE:** This is a builder's seat, not a manager's seat. You will write the ledger, the rails, and the reconciliation yourself. You will make the build\-versus\-buy call and defend it. You will tell the business no when correctness demands it, and you will be right often enough that they keep asking. The people who are great at this have owned a ledger somewhere it mattered, and they think in idempotency, race conditions, and reconciliation. **WHAT YOU'LL OWN:** * The ledger as system of record. Entries, lines, balances, holds, reversals, and the states between: pending, posted, available, canceled, declined, reversed. Immutability and audit trail as design constraints, not features. Point\-in\-time balances that show a customer where they stood on any past date. Done looks like an auditor pulling a trial balance without asking you for help. * Rails and money movement. ACH origination and returns, RTP and other instant rails, wires, cards, and stablecoin settlement. A credit\-push rail changes what you can auto\-charge and when funds are final, and you own those product consequences, not just the integration. Done looks like the fourth PSP costing a sprint, not a rewrite. * Reconciliation. When the ledger and the processor disagree, you own the answer. Automated matching, an exception queue a human can actually work, and breaks caught before a customer finds them. Every point of automation here is a point on the north star. * Payouts and lending infrastructure. Getting sellers and borrowers their money faster than anyone else in this market: instant payout options, batch payouts at auction close, and the settlement timing that makes them safe. Then the full loan lifecycle, disbursement through repayment, partial payment, delinquency, and collateral release. * Risk posture on high\-value flows. Holds, limits, and settlement windows set with data, and you will know what each one costs in conversion. Step\-up verification triggered by risk signals rather than blanket friction. * The trade\-off calls. Shipping speed against uncompromising correctness, build against buy. You set the planning cadence with Robbe, you work across Finance, Risk, Ops, and Support, and you are the one who explains upward why a number moved. **WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE IN 6 MONTHS:** * The reconciliation automation rate is materially higher than the day you started, and you can show the weekly series. * The exception queue at daily close is worked to zero by a human in under an hour, on a system you built for that. * A new rail or PSP has gone to production on the provider architecture you designed, and it did not require a ledger migration. * Pending, posted, and available are modeled cleanly enough that Support answers "where is my money" off the customer\-facing surface instead of escalating to engineering. * Corrections post as reversing entries. Nobody has edited history, and an auditor can say so. * At least one thing you shipped is running with AI in the loop, and the team depends on it. * Finance trusts the close. **HOW YOU'LL USE AI HERE** * Turn a payment provider or bank partner integration spec into a typed client and a test suite in an afternoon instead of a sprint, including the ACH return codes and reversal paths nobody wants to hand\-write. * Stand up a rail simulator that produces the failures a sandbox won't: a late return, a duplicate callback, a partial reversal, a webhook that arrives twice out of order, a settlement that lands after the window closed. Then run your ledger against it. * Build an agent that triages the reconciliation exception queue overnight, clusters the breaks, and hands you a ranked list with a proposed cause for each instead of a wall of unmatched rows. * Put an MCP server over the ledger so "where did this discrepancy come from" is a question you ask in plain language rather than another  real money on real rails. ACH origination and returns, RTP or FedNow, wires, or equivalent. You know what an R01 is, why NACHA return windows matter, and why a credit\-push rail changes the product flow and not just the API call. * You have handled large transactions, where the failure mode is a five\- or six\-figure problem and somebody notices immediately. * Database mastery. Expert SQL and relational design, and a transaction that holds under load at auction close and during scheduled auto\-pay batches. Python, Postgres, and AWS are our stack. * You're API\-native. Webhooks, idempotency, eventual consistency, and reconciliation are your default vocabulary, not terms you looked up. * You've built real things with AI, not just used it. Agents, skills, MCP servers, connectors, internal tooling people depend on. * Product\-owner thinking. You don't just build a pay button. You understand the flow of funds and how to tell a worried customer what happened to their money. * Restraint. The most common way this seat fails is overengineering. You know when a queue and a lambda are the answer and when they are three new partial\-failure modes. **We read the work, not the years. Most people who clear this bar have five to ten years behind them, and we have no interest in screening out the person who got there faster.** Strong plus: enough React and TypeScript to ship the customer\-facing surface that reads off your ledger. This is not a fullstack seat, but the person who can take a ledger change all the way to the UI will go further here. Backgrounds that fit: payments or ledger infrastructure at a pre\-IPO fintech, core banking or money movement at a marketplace, a founding or early engineer who built the money layer, or an infrastructure engineer who took ownership of financial correctness because nobody else would. Bonus: distributed systems, credit or risk modeling, direct experience with Stripe, Plaid, Airwallex, PayPal, Modern Treasury, or Increase, evaluating or implementing a third\-party ledger service (Modern Treasury, Fragment, Formance, TigerBeetle or similar), stablecoin or on\-chain settlement, KYC/KYB, bank partnership, or SOX and audit\-readiness exposure. You collect, or you have a view on where this market is going. US\-based, remote. **HOW WE'LL INTERVIEW YOU:** *We'll be specific so you can prepare. Before any of it: download the app, put a card up, make a bid, and try selling. Every round assumes you've used the product, and we expect your point of view to sharpen as you go. For this role, look specifically at the cash advance, deposit, and payout surfaces.* * Recruiter screen, 25 minutes, Google Meet. The metric you own today and how you're performing against it, why Alt specifically, and how you're actually using AI. We align on comp here and answer your questions. * Hiring manager, Robbe Simon, 45 minutes, Google Meet. * Technical screen, 60 minutes. * Architecture and system design, 60 minutes. * Culture interview, 30 minutes. How you work with the people who depend on your systems: operations, finance, support, and the customer on the other end of a held transfer. * Leore, our founder and CEO, 30 minutes. Everyone who joins Alt meets Leore. Come with a point of view on where you'd take Alt's ledger and money movement first. * Reference check(s), 15 minutes, with a former manager. **Compensation: $200,000 \- $500,000 per year, plus equity for all full\-time employees.** **What we offer:** ================== ***For full\-time Employees*** * We cover 85% of your medical, dental, and vision, and up to 50% for dependents. HSA/FSA available * Generous PTO that people actually take * Parental leave at full salary * $200/month wellness \+ $100/month home office stipend * Free DoorDash Pass membership, because dinner shouldn't be a decision * Remote\-first (for most positions), with WeWork access when you want a room with other humans * 401(k) * Alt Equity to all full\-time employees Compensation Range: $300K \- $500K

You’ll design and improve data systems across public cloud and SQL database environments, partnering with colleagues to deliver trusted, accessible data. **Duties** * Develop and maintain ETL (extract, transform, load) pipelines and data management integrations using tools such as Informatica, Talend, and Spark. * Design data warehouses, data models, and dimensional models; manage queries across Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, and cloud databases. * Work with AWS, Azure Data Lake, Hadoop, Apache Hive, and other big data systems to support data engineering and analytics. * Connect data sources through RESTful APIs and linked data approaches; support Looker and other business intelligence tools. * Your impact: By delivering well\-managed, dependable data, you help analytics and business teams make informed decisions. **Experience** * Strong data engineering and software development skills, including SQL and Python; Java is also useful. * Experience with ETL pipeline development, data warehousing design, database design, data modeling, and query management. * Familiarity with big data, public cloud, SQL databases, data warehouses, and business intelligence tools. * Agile experience, analysis skills, and working knowledge of Bash (Unix shell) or shell scripting. * Model training experience is a plus; equivalent experience with relevant tools and technologies is welcome. Pay: $112,000\.00 \- $137,000\.00 per year Benefits: * 401(k) Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Construction - Field Engineer
jobs.description: **Construction Field Engineer** **Position Summary** The Construction Field Engineer supports the superintendent and project manager in coordinating daily construction activities, reviewing project requirements, and tracking field progress. This position helps ensure work is completed safely, accurately, and in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, quality standards, and the project schedule. **Key Responsibilities** * Review drawings, specifications, approved submittals, and shop drawings to understand project requirements and identify discrepancies before installation. * Assist the superintendent with daily planning, subcontractor coordination, work sequencing, and jobsite logistics. * Prepare and track requests for information (RFIs), and communicate approved clarifications to affected field personnel. * Assist with construction layout and verify dimensions, elevations, locations, and existing conditions. * Observe installed work for conformance with contract documents; document deficiencies and track corrective actions. * Coordinate inspections and testing with subcontractors, testing agencies, and project leadership. * Maintain daily reports, progress photographs, field measurements, and records of manpower, equipment, deliveries, and significant jobsite events. * Track installed quantities and production progress to support schedule updates, cost reporting, and subcontractor payment reviews. * Monitor material deliveries and identify shortages, procurement delays, or other constraints that could affect field operations. * Maintain current drawings and field records, including redlines and information needed for record drawings. * Document potential scope changes and assist with quantity takeoffs and collection of supporting cost and schedule information. * Participate in coordination and safety meetings; promptly report unsafe conditions and project concerns. * Assist with punch lists, final inspections, turnover documentation, and project closeout. **Qualifications** * Degree in construction management, construction engineering, civil engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent field experience considered. * Previous construction experience or internship preferred. * Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and shop drawings. * Basic understanding of construction methods, materials, sequencing, and jobsite safety. * Strong organizational, communication, and problem\-solving skills. * Proficiency with Microsoft Office and familiarity with construction software such as Procore, Bluebeam, or similar platforms. * Familiarity with surveying and layout equipment is a plus. **Reporting and Working Conditions** Reports to the project manager and works under the superintendent’s direction for daily field activities. The position is primarily jobsite based and requires working outdoors, navigating active construction areas, and using required personal protective equipment. Travel and extended hours may be necessary depending on project needs. **Measures of Success** Accurate and timely field documentation, early identification of coordination issues, reliable progress tracking, effective subcontractor communication, and prompt follow\-through on assigned tasks. Pay: $70,000\.00 \- $110,000\.00 per year Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Senior Engineer II, Systems Engineering
jobs.description: US \> Arizona \> Phoenix **Step into a career with ASM, where cutting edge technology meets collaborative culture.** For over 55 years ASM has been ahead of what’s next, at the forefront of innovation and what’s technologically possible. With more than 4,500 ASMers representing 70 nationalities, our people and our advanced semiconductor devices are playing a crucial role in trends such as 5G, cloud computing, AI, and autonomous driving. But we’re more than just a tech company. We value diversity, inclusion and sustainability as we strive to make a positive impact on the world. Our development programs help support your growth, shaping your future and pushing the boundaries of innovation to unleash potential. **Job Mission** The Senior Engineer (II), Systems Engineering is a technical leader responsible for the development, integration, qualification, and deployment of advanced sensor technologies across ASM product platforms. This role focuses on transforming sensor data into actionable insights by driving sensor architecture, data acquisition strategies, signal analysis, and data\-driven decision\-making. Working closely with Mechanical, Electrical, Firmware, Software, Process, and Manufacturing Engineering teams, this individual will define sensor requirements, integrate sensing technologies into complex equipment, and develop analytical methods that improve process understanding, equipment performance, and product outcomes. This position requires strong systems thinking, expertise in sensor technologies and data analytics, and the ability to lead multidisciplinary projects from concept through deployment. **What You Will Be Working On** **Sensor Systems Leadership** * Lead the development and integration of advanced sensor technologies for semiconductor manufacturing equipment. * Define sensor architecture, performance requirements, interfaces, and validation strategies. * Evaluate and select sensing technologies for process monitoring, equipment health monitoring, and advanced control applications. * Drive sensor system design reviews focused on performance, scalability, and robustness. * Identify emerging sensor technologies and assess their applicability to future ASM products. **Sensor Integration \& Data Acquisition** * Lead integration of sensors with hardware, firmware, software, and control systems. * Develop and implement data acquisition architectures for collecting high\-quality sensor data. * Define calibration, synchronization, and validation methodologies for multi\-sensor systems. * Support integration of optical, thermal, pressure, flow, plasma, gas, vibration, acoustic, and environmental sensors. * Establish best practices for sensor characterization, performance evaluation, and deployment. **Data Analytics \& Insight Generation** * Develop data analysis methodologies to extract meaningful insights from sensor and equipment datasets. * Apply statistical analysis, signal processing, and machine learning techniques to identify patterns and correlations. * Analyze process and equipment data to improve product performance, process understanding, and operational efficiency. * Develop dashboards, KPIs, and health\-monitoring metrics for sensor\-enabled systems. * Generate data\-driven recommendations that influence product design and technology roadmaps. **Product Development \& Program Leadership** * Lead sensor technology development projects from concept through qualification and release. * Define verification and validation plans for sensor\-enabled subsystems. * Drive proof\-of\-concept studies and technology demonstrations for next\-generation sensing solutions. * Coordinate technical activities across multiple development programs and stakeholders. * Collaborate with suppliers and technology partners to evaluate and qualify new sensor solutions. **Cross\-Functional Collaboration** * Partner with Process, Software, Firmware, Electrical, Mechanical, and Product Engineering teams to deploy sensor solutions. * Work closely with data scientists and software engineers to operationalize sensor data. * Support customer\-facing activities requiring sensor characterization, performance analysis, and technology assessments. * Present technical findings and recommendations to engineering leadership and business stakeholders. **Mentorship \& Technical Leadership** * Mentor engineers in sensor technologies, systems engineering, and data analytics methodologies. * Promote best practices for sensor integration, experimental design, and data analysis. * Lead technical working groups focused on sensor innovation and advanced monitoring capabilities. * Drive continuous improvement in sensor development processes and analytical workflows. **Minimum Qualifications** * BS in Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Physics, Optical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical discipline. * 5\+ years of experience in sensor systems, system integration, data acquisition, process diagnostics, or related engineering functions. * Experience integrating sensors into complex hardware systems. * Experience with data analysis, signal processing, and statistical methods. * Proficiency with data analysis tools such as Python, MATLAB, JMP, Minitab, or similar platforms. * Experience designing and executing experiments for sensor characterization and validation. * Strong systems\-level problem\-solving and troubleshooting skills. * Excellent communication and cross\-functional collaboration skills. **Preferred Qualifications** * MS or PhD in Engineering, Physics, Data Science, or related technical field. * Experience with semiconductor equipment and semiconductor manufacturing processes. * Experience with optical sensors, spectroscopy, machine vision, imaging systems, gas sensing, plasma diagnostics, or environmental monitoring. * Experience with edge computing, Industrial IoT, and connected sensor systems. * Experience with machine learning, predictive analytics, and large\-scale data processing. * Experience developing sensor\-driven control strategies and process monitoring solutions. * Knowledge of database systems, cloud analytics platforms, and data infrastructure. **What Makes You Successful** * Strong understanding of sensor technologies and how to translate measurements into actionable information. * Ability to connect sensor data, process behavior, and equipment performance. * Passion for data\-driven engineering and advanced analytics. * Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary technical projects. * Excellent troubleshooting and root\-cause analysis skills. * Strong collaboration and stakeholder management abilities. * Demonstrated ownership, innovation, and continuous improvement mindset. **Apply today to be part of what’s next.** We make the tech that enables the chips in devices which improve lives around the world. We do this with an eye to the future, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible through cutting\-edge innovation, and driving the next wave of technological breakthroughs that shape how we live, work, and connect. To learn more about ASM, find us at asm.com and on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube. *ASM is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, nationality, social or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender, gender identify or expression, marital status, pregnancy, political affiliation, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.*

jobs.title: [CSP] Site Reliability Engineer (14:00–22:00 CET)
jobs.description: Communications Service Providers (CSP) are the biggest, most important clients of AVSystem. We build, test, launch and operate systems for our telco customers and make a living by keeping them relevant, reliable and remarkable. Our products (UMP, CEM, BSAP and DHCP) manage hundreds of millions of devices in 100\+ large deployments worldwide, for operators like T\-Mobile, Play and Vodafone, also through our cloud offering. The SRE team runs them on Kubernetes in GCP and AWS, on bare metal and VMs in operators' data centres, and in air\-gapped on\-prem environments. Every operator brings its own customizations, and years of per\-operator projects left debt in our tooling, processes and infrastructure. You'll spend part of your time untangling and simplifying it, which takes discipline. Running the commands was never the hard part of this job. Deciding which ones to run was, and owning the result: whether a change is safe on an operator's network, what to fix first when two customers call at once, and when a workaround can wait until morning. We are looking for an engineer who takes those decisions and carries them, with whatever tools write the scripts this year. ### **Your hours** This role works a fixed afternoon schedule: **14:00–22:00 CET**, **Monday** **to** **Friday**, so our operators in the US and Latin America have an SRE inside their working day, and planned work that fits these hours goes to you, whichever time zone the operator is in. Those hours are your normal working time, not overtime. You'll spend your first weeks in daytime hours next to the team, then move to the afternoon schedule. Each day starts with a handover from the daytime team and ends with a written note for the morning. **Requirements** ---------------- * A few years running production Linux systems as an **SRE**, **DevOps** engineer or **sysadmin**, with solid **Linux** (Ubuntu, RHEL) and **networking** (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, routing) fundamentals: from a shell, you can tell what a host is doing and why. * **Python** or Go good enough to write automation your teammates can read, test and maintain. Bash for the small things. * Working knowledge of **Kubernetes**, at least one public cloud (**GCP**, **AWS** or **Azure**), and **Ansible** or Terraform. * Hands\-on monitoring, alerting and logging work with the **Prometheus** **stack** and Loki, which we run, or with Zabbix, Splunk or ELK. * Daily, hands\-on use of coding agents (we run **Claude** **Code**), the judgment to tell when their output is wrong, and the habit of not running in production what you could not explain to a colleague. * Fluent spoken **English** (you will often run calls with our customers' teams on your own, native speakers included) and proficiency in Polish. **A huge plus if you have** --------------------------- * Set up and run MongoDB, Redis or Kafka. * Tuned or debugged JVM applications and distributed systems. * Supported customers in another time zone, or worked shifts. * Readiness to travel to our customers in the US from time to time. **Not for you if** ------------------ * you need your weekday evenings free. * you think customer calls are someone else's job. * your first move on a slow service is a restart, not a graph. * you would rather repeat a manual task than automate it. * you want every runbook written before you touch a system. **Responsibilities** -------------------- * Own problems end to end: frame them, choose the approach, direct agents and teammates through the implementation, verify the result, and run it in production. * Learn the telco domain on purpose: how an operator runs its access network, what our products do in it, and what a failed rollout costs the operator. * Work with our US and Latin American customers during their day, from calls and troubleshooting with their engineers to resolving production issues, and run any operator's planned work (upgrades, migrations, configuration changes) that fits your hours. * Build and maintain automation that removes toil from the team's week. * Find and fix performance and reliability problems, including in our product code, and lead the blameless postmortems that keep them from coming back. * Improve our observability stack (Prometheus, Loki, Grafana) and the Service Level Indicators the team watches. * Work with development teams on feature design, so they ship features we can operate. * After onboarding, join our additionally paid 24/7 on\-call rotation. **How we hire** --------------- * A call with our recruiter, partly in English, with a few short technical questions. * Three technical conversations with the SRE team, online: Linux troubleshooting on a live VM, a short Python exercise, and system design. * A conversation with the team's manager. We send the meeting link and the format of each stage before every interview. Take a break whenever you need one. **What we offer** ----------------- * Remote work from anywhere **in Poland**, with occasional visits to our Kraków office. * Our goal is to inspire people more than manage them. We want our teams to do what is best for our products. This, in turn, generates a **sense of responsibility** which drives us to do great work. * A dream team is one in which all of your colleagues are extraordinary at what they do and highly effective working together. We model ourselves on a professional sports team, not a family. A family is about unconditional love. A dream team is about pushing yourself to be the best possible teammate. **Dream** **teams** are about **performance**, not seniority or tenure. * Our customers depend on the reliability of our products to generate revenue in their business. The telco industry is ever\-growing and needs us to support that growth. * Open\-source contribution opportunities. * A team of highly skilled and humorous colleagues. * Access to the best tools and equipment available in the market. * A **Claude Code Premium seat** from day one and the model access the work needs. We don't ration tokens; we look at what shipped. * A MacBook Pro / ThinkPad with 2 monitors. * Company events and team building activities. * Multiple career paths and employee development options – we want you to develop into a tech lead in the future, but we’ll support you in getting another dream role in site reliability, management, product development or sales. * Training and conferences. * Onsite gym and chillout space. * Multisport card. * Medical care. * Kitchen full of snacks and treats (including Good Lood ice cream). * Car parking area and bike room. * A relaxed work atmosphere – no dress code, no open space. ##### **Site Reliability Engineer** Product: CSP Level: Regular Contract: B2B/ UoP Location: Remote Salary UoP: 16 600 \- 24 900 Salary B2B: 20 000 \- 30 000 Holiday: 20\+ paid days
